title: Work: The Dot Product at Play

steps.body:
In physics, **work** = force · displacement — literally the dot product:

W = F · d.

Only the part of the force ALONG the motion does work. A force ⟨6, 8⟩ N moving an object ⟨10, 0⟩ m does W = 6·10 + 8·0 = **60 joules** — the vertical 8 contributes nothing to horizontal motion.
Work counts only the part of the force that goes your way.

widget.prompt: A cart moves 4 m east: u = (4, 0). Steer the force v until the work (the dot product) reads 12.
widget.successFeedback: v = (3, 3) gives 4(3) + 0(3) = 12. Only the EASTWARD part of the force did any work — the upward 3 contributed exactly nothing, because the cart never went up. That is why work is a dot product and not a plain multiplication.
widget.lowFeedback: The work is under 12. Only the horizontal part of the force counts, so push more to the east.
widget.highFeedback: The work is over 12. The eastward component of the force is doing all of it — ease it back.

predict.prompt: Look at the two arrows before you move anything. The dot product u · v of the STARTING pair is…

options.label: Positive — they lean the same way

predict.reveal: u · v = 4·0 + 0·3 = 0. One number tells the geometry: positive means the angle is under 90°, zero means exactly 90°, negative means past it.

cml.actionGoal: Change vector components and coordinate geometric movement with component and dot-product representations.

explanationVariants: A force ⟨0, 5⟩ moving an object ⟨4, 0⟩ does W = 0·4 + 5·0 = 0 — perpendicular force does NO work.
Carrying a bag horizontally: gravity (down) does zero work on horizontal motion.

widget.prompt: A vertical force ⟨0, 5⟩ N moves an object horizontally along ⟨4, 0⟩ m. How much work is done? (Joules.)

numericErrors.feedback: 20 = 5·4 multiplies the wrong parts. W = 0·4 + 5·0 = 0 — the force is perpendicular to the motion.
9 = 5 + 4 adds. Work is the dot product: 0·4 + 5·0 = 0 J.

widget.explorationFeedback: Inspect the required exact-number states before checking.
widget.fallbackFeedback: Perpendicular force does zero work: W = 0 J.
widget.successFeedback: Perpendicular force does zero work: W = 0 J.

steps.body: The **projection** idea underlies this: u · v = |u| |v| cos θ picks out the shadow of one vector on the other. When they align (θ = 0°), the dot product is maximal (full |u||v|); at 90° it's zero. Work measures exactly the force's shadow along the path.

explanationVariants: A force ⟨5, 0⟩ along motion ⟨3, 0⟩ does W = 15 J — fully aligned, no wasted component.
When force and motion share a direction, all the force does work: 5·3 = 15 J.

widget.prompt: A force ⟨5, 0⟩ N moves an object ⟨3, 0⟩ m (same direction). Find the work, in joules.

numericErrors.feedback: 8 = 5 + 3 adds. Work is the dot product: 5·3 + 0·0 = 15 J.
Here force and motion ALIGN, so work is maximal: 5·3 = 15 J, not 0.

widget.explorationFeedback: Inspect the required exact-number states before checking.

explanationVariants: F = ⟨3, 4⟩ along d = ⟨5, 0⟩: W = 3·5 + 4·0 = 15 J — only the horizontal 3 does work.
The 4 (vertical) is perpendicular to the motion and contributes nothing: 15 J.

widget.prompt: A force ⟨3, 4⟩ N moves an object along ⟨5, 0⟩ m. What is the work, in joules?

numericErrors.feedback: 35 = 3·5 + 4·5 wrongly pairs 4 with 5. d's y-component is 0: W = 15 + 0 = 15 J.
20 = 4·5 uses the wrong component. Along ⟨5, 0⟩: W = 3·5 = 15 J.

widget.explorationFeedback: Inspect the required exact-number states before checking.

explanationVariants: A friction force ⟨−4, 0⟩ opposing motion ⟨6, 0⟩ does W = −24 J — negative, because the force fights the motion.
Force opposite to displacement gives negative work: −4·6 = −24 J.
hints: Work is still F · d, signs included.
A force opposing motion does NEGATIVE work.

widget.prompt: Friction ⟨−4, 0⟩ N acts as an object moves ⟨6, 0⟩ m. What is the work done by friction, in joules?

numericErrors.feedback: Friction OPPOSES motion, so the work is negative: (−4)(6) = −24 J.
2 = −4 + 6 adds. Work is the dot product: (−4)(6) = −24 J.

widget.explorationFeedback: Inspect the required exact-number states before checking.

takeaways: Work W = F · d — only the force component along the motion counts.
Perpendicular force → zero work; aligned → maximal; opposing → negative.
The dot product u·v = |u||v|cos θ measures one vector's shadow on the other.

concept.body: Work W = F · d = (dot product). Perpendicular force does zero work; force opposing motion does negative work.

widget.prompt: A force ⟨2, 0⟩ N moves an object ⟨7, 0⟩ m. Find the work, in joules.

commonErrors.feedback: 9 = 2 + 7 adds. Work is the dot product: 2·7 = 14 J.
Force and motion align, so work is 2·7 = 14 J, not 0.
